title: Parts Per Million (ppm) / Parts Per Billion (ppb)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

expression: ppm = (mass of solute / mass of solution) × 10⁶  (for dilute aqueous solutions, approximated as mg/L)
explanation: Expresses very low concentrations as a ratio scaled by one million (ppm) or one billion (ppb). For dilute aqueous solutions, where 1 L of solution has a mass close to 1 kg, ppm is commonly approximated as mg/L — a simplification that becomes less accurate for concentrated or non-aqueous solutions.

workedExample.scenario: 5 mg of solute dissolved in 1 L of dilute aqueous solution.

commonMistakes: Applying the mg/L ≈ ppm shortcut to a concentrated or non-aqueous solution, where the density assumption it relies on no longer holds.
